rationale: ary3 is a tiny (512-byte text, 2 functions) Shootout benchmark dominated by a single hot integer array-index loop, so the table strongly favors cheap, loop-safe transformations and suppresses expensive control-flow ones: SUB and IGV get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain with low RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights because instruction substitution and constant/global-value masking obscure the arithmetic core with minimal steady-state overhead, and SPLIT adds basic-block diversity almost for free on this micro-sized function set. BCF and FLA carry high RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights so the selector effectively disables or minimizes them — bogus control flow and flattening would balloon a 512-byte binary and devastate a benchmark whose entire body is a hot loop. IBR sits at moderate weights since indirect-branch rewriting hinders static analysis but adds indirect-branch predictor pressure in the hot loop, while ICALL gets moderate weights with an elevated CorrectnessRisk given the sparse call structure where indirect-call conversion yields little and risks visibility into the few existing calls. CorrectnessRisk is kept low across the board except for FLA/ICALL because this program's correctness hinges on tight loop semantics with few places for restructuring to go wrong.
